title: Block gallery
summary: Vocabulary sheet for all 19 Showmob blocks, plus a few starter recipes as grammar suggestions—not required slots.

blocks.title: Block gallery
blocks.body: This page is the vocabulary-and-grammar sheet for Showmob. Layer one shows every block type once. Layer two shows a few starter recipes—named combinations that do a job. Recipes are suggestions under gradient judgment: choose among them and drop empty blocks. They are never required slots to fill.

blocks.title: How to read this page
blocks.body: Each specimen is live renderer output. The short note beside it is the recipe hint for that type. An auto-check in tests asserts every schema block type appears at least once here, so coverage cannot quietly fall behind.

blocks.heading: hero — page orientation
blocks.body: Recipe: open with one hero. Short title, clear body, optional eyebrow. Prefer a single hero per page.

blocks.title: Follow the strongest signal
blocks.body: A hero orients the reader before any other block. Keep it short enough to scan.

blocks.title: text — one explanation
blocks.body: Recipe: one heading, one body. Split long prose into multiple text blocks instead of stuffing paragraphs.

blocks.heading: Name the reference
blocks.body: A text block holds one idea. The renderer treats the body as a single paragraph of ordinary text—no Markdown parsing.

blocks.heading: stat-strip — sourced figures
blocks.body: Recipe: a few labeled values the reader should remember. Format numbers as strings; labels carry units and scope.

blocks.heading: steps — ordered sequence
blocks.body: Recipe: numbered list when order matters. Keep each step one action.

blocks.heading: comparison — alternatives side by side
blocks.body: Recipe: two or more columns with name + detail. Keep details comparable.

blocks.heading: quote — attributable line
blocks.body: Recipe: short quote plus attribution. Do not invent a source.

blocks.quote: Record what you can actually support.

blocks.heading: note-callout — limit, tip, or warning
blocks.body: Recipe: title + body; optional tone note | positive | warning. Say the meaning in words, not only color.

blocks.title: Paper example
blocks.body: These values explain a principle, not a hardware specification.

blocks.heading: cta-band — closing action as text
blocks.body: Recipe: heading + body that name what to do next. Not a button or link.

blocks.heading: Explain it once
blocks.body: Write the distinction in your own words before opening another page.

blocks.heading: checklist — temporary self-check
blocks.body: Recipe: labels the reader can toggle locally. Selections are not saved evidence of completion.

items.label: Name the reference
items.detail: Say what the voltage is relative to.

blocks.heading: timeline — chronology
blocks.body: Recipe: time, title, detail in authored order. The renderer does not sort dates.

blocks.title: choice
blocks.body: A radio group for "pick one" copy: one selection replaces the last, tapping the selection clears it. Session-local, resets on unmount.

items.label: First option
items.detail: Selecting this replaces any other pick.

items.label: Second option
items.detail: Tap again to clear your pick.

blocks.heading: fill-in — worksheet blanks
blocks.body: Recipe: labeled blanks the reader types into. Entries are session-local, never checked or transmitted.

blocks.heading: reveal — hidden until asked
blocks.body: Recipe: content the reader must explicitly open, like an answer key. The button toggles the panel.

blocks.heading: A hidden fact
blocks.label: Show the fact
blocks.body: This sentence only renders after the reader asks for it.

blocks.heading: code — literal data to read
blocks.body: Recipe: heading + code string. Optional language is retained but not highlighted. Nothing executes.

blocks.heading: embed — source / reference card
blocks.body: Recipe: heading, source name, caption; optional absolute HTTPS URL. Renders a card, not an iframe.

blocks.heading: Repository source: contribution rules
blocks.caption: Review, validation, and link-handoff expectations for changes.

blocks.heading: image — authored visual
blocks.body: Recipe: src (repo path or HTTPS), alt, caption; optional heading. Prefer repository assets.

blocks.heading: A separated lab
blocks.alt: An upstream network connects to a lab router that separates trusted devices, a passive sensor, and an isolated honeypot with blocked outbound access.
blocks.caption: Existing public asset used as the image specimen.

blocks.heading: resource-list — curated next steps
blocks.body: Recipe: label, detail, absolute HTTPS url per item.

items.label: Showmob widgets catalog
items.detail: Authoring contract for every block type.

blocks.heading: exercise — check understanding
blocks.body: Recipe: prompt, options, zero-based answer index, explanation. Feedback strings are optional.

blocks.heading: Check the model
blocks.explanation: Voltage describes a difference between two points.

blocks.heading: compact-table — small grid
blocks.body: Recipe: columns + rows of strings; optional caption. Keep cells short.

blocks.heading: diagram — process nodes
blocks.body: Recipe: ordered nodes with title + detail. Good for flows, not free-form graphs.

blocks.heading: slideshow — paced slides in-page
blocks.body: Recipe: heading + slides with title and body. Browse remains the whole page; present inside the block.

slides.title: Present in place
slides.body: Use the block controls when pacing helps.

blocks.heading: divider — section break
blocks.body: Recipe: optional label. Use to name major sections without another heading block.

blocks.heading: Starter recipes (suggestions)
blocks.body: Named combinations that do a job. Re-using block types here is expected. Gradient judgment picks among recipes and drops what the content does not need—never treat these as mandatory section lists.

blocks.title: Separate world from telling
blocks.body: World pages hold facts that should stay consistent. Telling is ordered prose written against those pages.

blocks.heading: Why the split matters
blocks.body: AI is strong at prose and weak at long-range consistency. Keep character and place facts on pages; update them after scenes ship. Updates stay human-reviewed for now.

nodes.title: Read world pages
nodes.detail: Before a scene, open what it touches.

blocks.heading: Quick check
blocks.prompt: Where should lasting character facts live?
options: On world pages in the site
blocks.explanation: World pages are the source of truth; prose is written against them.

blocks.title: Caveat
blocks.body: Do not expand the schema for importance markers until a real page demands them. The test is whether the agent picks blocks from content pressure or fills a pattern.

blocks.heading: First five minutes on unfamiliar gear
items: Stop at the boundary and read labels.
Ask what changed since the last normal cycle.
Watch one full cycle without intervening.

items.title: Boundary
items.detail: Energy sources and guards before entry.

items.title: Decide
items.detail: One safe check, not a speculative repair.

blocks.heading: Carry one sentence forward
blocks.body: If you can state the next check in one sentence, the beat is done.
